rationale: Published by OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync (Acme.Orders) and handled by OrderPlacedWorker (Acme.Orders.Worker) -- producer, type and consumer prove the identity is shared across a project boundary. Already proven by ContractRelationIntegrationTests. Contract identity is proven, so both the producer and the consumer must be recoverable from postings in one hop from that identity (GCPC-091). Note: Certification.Messaging/ContractShapes.cs's OrderCreated is published and handled entirely within one project (Certification.Messaging), which ContractPass does not promote to a Contract -- that pair is deliberately not used as the positive case here; see T54's commit deviation note.

Published with deliberately no handler anywhere in the corpus. Must publish an explicit unresolved or excluded outcome, never a contract, and must never be presented in any envelope as 'no messaging' (GCPC-089, GCPC-092).

Certification.Messaging.Receipt and Certification.Api.Receipt share a name but nothing else -- no project reference either way. The classifier must never create a shared contract identity from name similarity, structural similarity, path or prefix alone (GCPC-090); the expected 'absent' is the absence of a shared contract across the pair, not the absence of either individual type.
